soft-01.note: PIB release posted 04 MAY 2025 11:30AM. Both quoted sentences appear verbatim. The release says ECINET 'will integrate and reorient' over 40 apps and that the Commission 'is developing' it, so 'replace' overstated the release and the platform was announced as under development. The audience in the release is 'electors and its other stakeholders such as the election officials, political parties and the civil society'.
soft-01.claim: The Commission announced in May 2025 that it was building ECINET, one platform to bring together more than 40 of its apps and websites for voters, election officials and other users.

soft-02.note: PIB release 'ECINET Digital Platform launched at IICDEM-2026', posted 22 JAN 2026 8:17PM. 'today launched ECINET' and the beta sentence appear verbatim. The listed URL (with &reg=6&lang=1) returns the page shell without the body to a plain request; the same release reads in full at https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2217429.

soft-03.note: TNIE, 24 January 2026 (datePublished 2026-01-24). Both quoted passages appear verbatim. The article also says an ERO reported that 'no user-manuals were provided for the updates' and that officials relied heavily on the app to understand the tasks, which supports the claim. The district-level official is unnamed.

soft-04.note: Same TNIE article. Sentence appears verbatim. The BLO is unnamed in the source and in the claim.

soft-05.note: Free Press Journal, Bhopal, 18 November 2025. Quote verbatim, attributed by the paper to the BLOs as a group in Bhopal city. A BLO and a voter are named elsewhere in the story; neither is used here.

soft-06.note: Deccan Chronicle, 22 July 2026 (published 23:02 IST; the glitch was 'on Wednesday', 22 July). Quote verbatim. Users 'refreshing the page redirected them back to the home screen'. The RTI activist and the advocate quoted by the paper are not named in the claim, correctly.

soft-07.note: The Reporters' Collective, dated February 8, 2026 on the page. Quote matches verbatim (the list items run together as on the page). The article says 'we sent detailed questions to the ECI. We had not received an answer by the time of publication', which supports the response.

soft-08.note: Quote verbatim. The ERO said the button was there 'Till this morning', so it disappeared during that day, not overnight. The ERO is unnamed in source and claim.
soft-08.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that a registration officer showed its reporter that the button to clear voters with a name mismatch had disappeared from ERONET since that morning, so such cases now needed the district officer's approval.

soft-09.note: Quote verbatim. The article says 'the district magistrates of at least three districts wrote to the West Bengal CEO's office' and then 'Having received no response from the ECI, they continued with their internal methods regardless', which supports the response. District magistrates acting in office; none is named.

soft-10.note: Quote verbatim, including 'The Collective could not independently verify this claim.' The preceding paragraph says the oral instruction came from the West Bengal CEO when hearings were first instituted, which supports the claim. ERO unnamed.

soft-11.note: The Reporters' Collective, dated January 14, 2026 on the page. Both fragments verbatim. The article says the group comprised the CEO and the district magistrates, that TMC first alleged this in a plea by its Parliamentary Party Leader before the Supreme Court, and that 'The ECI and the CEO of West Bengal did not reply to our detailed queries pertaining to the use of WhatsApp'.

soft-12.note: Quote verbatim, and the article reproduces the CEO office's letter. The only stated non-reply is to queries 'pertaining to the use of WhatsApp' and to whether the WhatsApp orders were put on record, so the response is narrowed to what the source says.
soft-12.response: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

soft-13.note: Supreme Court record of proceedings dated 19-01-2026, W.P.(C) 1089/2025 with connected matters (SIR matters related to West Bengal). Quote verbatim. The order states the logical discrepancy category accounts 'for approximately 1.36 crore voters'.

soft-14.note: Siasat, published 19 January 2026 1:50 pm IST, is an IANS wire copy (byline 'Indo-Asian News Service'). Quote verbatim, attributed to 'an official from the CEO's office'. The claim that people had 'falsely linked themselves' is the officials' assertion and is now attributed to them through IANS. The outlet field should read 'Siasat (IANS, citing officials of the CEO West Bengal)'.
soft-14.claim: Officials of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told IANS that the logical discrepancy check caught people who had falsely linked themselves to unrelated voters, and gave examples they said were found at hearings.
soft-14.outlet: Siasat (IANS, citing officials of the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal)

soft-15.note: CEO Meghalaya press note No.EL.63/2026/50 dated Shillong, 18 August 2026. The PDF text layer is OCR with letter errors ('eLector', 'tess'), but read line by line it carries all six checks in the quoted wording. The note is about SIR 2026 notices, which is the third phase.

soft-16.note: TNIE, PTI copy, datePublished 2026-06-07. Quote verbatim. The article says phase III was launched on May 14, so the instructions circulated that day are for the third phase.

soft-17.note: The Hindu, 4 October 2026 (published 18:25 IST). Quote verbatim from 'an ERO, who did not wish to be named', speaking of the enumeration phase in Delhi. The paper's only stated non-response is 'The Delhi CEO's office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage', so the response is narrowed to that.
soft-17.response: The Delhi CEO's office and the EC did not respond to The Hindu's queries on why the new ERONET options were introduced at that stage.

soft-18.note: Same Hindu article. Opening paragraph verbatim, attributed to sources. The eight-minute length is stated later in the article. Response sentence verbatim in substance.

soft-19.note: Both fragments verbatim. The article says the options are available in 'the remaining 10 States and Union Territories (UTs) where the third phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is still under way', and separately that 'The notice phase is under way in only nine States', so 'ten still in the notice phase' misstated the source.
soft-19.claim: The Hindu reported that the options reached Delhi officers on 30 September and only the ten states and union territories where the third phase was still under way, and that a case marked ineligible still could not be reversed.

soft-20.note: The Hindu, Delhi, published 27 September 2026. The quote is the article's standfirst, verbatim. The lede says the Delhi CEO's letter of Friday 25 September 2026 set a 10-point checklist and told officers no deletion should be made on 'flimsy or frivolous grounds'. Only the standfirst and lede are public, and they carry everything the item uses.

soft-21.note: The Indian Express, 6 October 2026. Quote verbatim from the 11 August minutes. The article says the portal did not allow tribunals to serve notices, hold virtual hearings, restore a deleted voter, or let appellants download orders, and that the paper emailed the ECI and the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court on 1 October with no response.

soft-22.note: Outlook, 29 September 2026, citing NDTV. Quote verbatim. The Commission's 26 September statement is reported in the article and matches the PIB release in soft-27. The NDTV original is not in the file, so the rewrite stands, though the NDTV report would be the better source if it is found.

soft-23.note: Hindustan Times, published 8 October 2026. Facts check out: email to CERT-In on 8 July copied to the ECI complaints address, the critical finding, CERT-In's reply of 6 October about the hardcoded AES key he rated of least concern, 'HT sent its questions to both bodies on October 5. Neither responded.', 'none of the flaws ... were directly related to this', and 'The email alleges no theft or misuse of data.' The researcher is a private individual and was named in claim, quote and response. Name replaced with the role; in the quote the replacement is bracketed.
soft-23.claim: Hindustan Times reported that a security researcher emailed CERT-In on 8 July 2026, copied to the Commission's complaints address, about flaws in the voter-services website and the ECINET app. The worst, in the researcher's account, let anyone obtain election officials' names and mobile numbers without logging in.
soft-23.quote: The issue [the researcher] rated as critical concerns a server behind the voter portal. He says it returned the names and mobile numbers of election officials to requests that carried no login, CAPTCHA or visible limit on the number of requests.
soft-23.response: HT said neither CERT-In nor the Commission answered its questions of 5 October. On 6 October CERT-In told the researcher that one flaw, the hardcoded encryption key he rated least serious, had been fixed and that work on the rest was under progress. HT said none of the flaws related directly to registration officers' access to the roll, and that the email alleged no theft or misuse of data.

soft-24.note: Scroll, published 8 October 2026 ('on Thursday'). Quote verbatim. Scroll names the researcher; the item does not. The second sentence of the claim said the HT report 'did not link the security flaws to it', which Scroll does not say. It is now tied to what HT itself said (see soft-23). Scroll reports no Commission response.
soft-24.claim: Congress alleged after the Hindustan Times report that ECINET was designed to centralise deletions and additions from the BJP's headquarters. This is a party's allegation. Hindustan Times had said none of the flaws it reported related directly to registration officers' access to the roll.

soft-25.note: ThePrint, PTI feed, New Delhi, Oct 2 2026. Quote verbatim, Jairam Ramesh speaking as Congress general secretary (public official, attributed by name). The Commission statement PTI cites was its answer to the objections of two Election Commissioners, not to Ramesh's ECINet charge, so the response now says so.
soft-25.response: PTI recalled that the Commission, under fire over objections from two of its Commissioners, had said differing views are a normal part of deliberation and that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

soft-26.note: The Pioneer, dated September 25, 2026 (officials spoke 'on Thursday', 24 September). Both fragments verbatim. The article says field officers act through unique IDs and passwords and that ERONET has been integrated into ECINet.

soft-27.note: PIB release posted 26 SEP 2026 5:36PM; meeting held 26.09.2026 at 3:00 PM with the approval of the full Commission. Both fragments verbatim.
